slides.text: An `if` picks which code runs. The condition must be a `bool`, it has no parentheses, and the braces are always required.

In Rust an `if` is also an expression: it can produce a value. This module covers both uses.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Rust.
slides.code:
if the condition is true
    do this
otherwise if another is true
    do that
otherwise
    do the other

exercises.title: If and else
exercises.guide: Choose between two paths with `if` and `else`.

chunks.guide: The block after `if` runs when the condition is true. Otherwise the block after `else` runs.

notes.text: Runs the block when the check was false.

chunks.guide: Two more checks: `==` tests for equal, `<` for less than.

notes.text: Two equal signs compare. One would assign.

chunks.guide: This line runs whichever path was taken.

exercises.title: Complete the chain
exercises.guide: Label a stock level: 0 is `sold out`, 3 is `low`, 5 is `ok`. Stock is 5 now, so it must print `ok`.

exercises.title: Several choices
exercises.guide: Pick one of four paths with an `else if` chain.

chunks.guide: The checks run from the top. The first true one runs its block and the rest are skipped. `else` catches what is left.

notes.text: Tried only if the checks above were false.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `n > 5` is true, so its block runs and the chain stops there. `n > 10` is never checked.

exercises.title: Combined conditions
exercises.guide: Keep a check in a variable and join checks with `&&` and `||`.

chunks.guide: A comparison gives a `bool`, so it can be stored and used as a condition. `&&` needs both sides true.

notes.text: True only when both sides are true.

chunks.guide: `||` needs only one side true. With no `else`, a false check prints nothing.

output.text:
slow down, wet road
lights on

slides.text:
Every branch of an `if` is a block, and a block gives the value of its last line when that line has no `;`.

So the whole `if` can be the value. Pseudo code:
Because the `if` has one value, all its branches must give the same type, and an `else` is required.

exercises.title: An if with a value
exercises.guide: Store the result of an `if` in a variable.

chunks.guide: An `if` is an expression: the block that runs gives its last line as the value. Leave out the `;` on that line.

notes.text: No semicolon: this line is the branch's value.

exercises.title: Complete the value
exercises.guide: A fighter at 0 hp stays down, one at 5 hp gets 2 more. With `hp` at 0 it must print 0.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Work out which branch gives the value, then use it.
exercises.explanation: `lives > 0` is false, so the `else` branch gives 5 as the value of the `if`. Then `bonus * 2` is 10.

exercises.title: Statements before the value
exercises.guide: A branch can do some work before it gives its value.

chunks.guide: A branch is a block: it can hold statements, and its last line without `;` is the value.

exercises.title: An if inside println
exercises.guide: Use an `if` directly as an argument.

chunks.guide: An `if` expression can sit wherever a value fits, like an argument of `println!`.

exercises.title: An if inside an if
exercises.guide: Put a second check inside a branch.

chunks.guide: The inner `if` runs only when the outer check is true.

exercises.title: A tuple from an if
exercises.guide: Sort two numbers by giving back a tuple.

chunks.guide: A branch can give any value, here a tuple. Both branches give the same shape, and `let` unpacks it.

notes.text: The tuple is the value of this branch.

exercises.title: Cap a value
exercises.guide: Cap `level` at `max`: a raw 150 shows 100, a raw 40 shows 40.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.explanation: The two `if`s are separate. The first prints `A`. In the second, `n > 10` is true, so it prints `B` and the `else` is skipped.

exercises.title: Most specific first
exercises.guide: Order the checks so the narrowest one comes first.

chunks.guide: A multiple of 15 is also a multiple of 3 and 5, so that check must come first, or it would never be reached.
